$comment: Which GL constants the WebGL boundary names, and for the ones content cannot name, why.
Derived half: scripts/test-webgl-constant-reach-contract.sh parses every `glow::CONST`
out of each source below and intersects that with glow's own `pub const NAME: u32` set,
so a type name like `glow::Context` cannot leak in as the constant `C`. Whatever survives
is a GL enum the engine can hand to, or accept from, content.
Classified half: this file, because it cannot be derived. A constant the engine uses for
an internal GLES call is not necessarily part of WebGL's surface -- WebGL wraps some of
them in a friendlier API and exposes no enum at all. Four such, and only four across all
six sources, which is what makes this file readable enough to be worth reading.
WHY THIS EXISTS: a missing constant is not an error, it is a silent wrong branch, and
01_constants.js has now paid for it five times.
1. `UNIFORM_BUFFER` absent -- a UBO upload targeted `undefined`, nothing was visible.
2. `INVALID_INDEX` absent -- the documented `if (index === gl.INVALID_INDEX)` never
took that branch.
3. the WebGL 2 sync set absent -- `fenceSync(gl.SYNC_GPU_COMMANDS_COMPLETE, 0)` passed
`undefined` as the fence condition.
4. `DRAW_FRAMEBUFFER` absent -- `blitFramebuffer` is implemented and reachable only by
binding that target, so the blit path was dead code.
5. 48 sized internal formats absent -- six methods that take one are implemented and
only RGB8 and RGBA8 were declared, so `texStorage2D(t, 1, gl.RGBA16F, w, h)` passed
`undefined`. Plus TEXTURE_BASE_LEVEL/TEXTURE_MAX_LEVEL for texParameteri.
The first three were each found by someone tripping over the consequence. The fourth was
found by running this derivation by hand over one source; the fifth by widening it, which
is the only reason it was found at all rather than in a sixth bug report.
The SOURCE LIST is derived too, and that is the second lesson. The first version listed
the six boundary sources and checked each one named something -- but deleting a line from
that list dropped coverage from 132 constants to 77 and still passed green. A gate that
cannot notice its own scope shrinking is the exact failure mode it was written to prevent,
one level up. So every file under graphics/src that names a glow constant must appear in
`sources` or in `internal_only`, and a file in neither fails. Dropping a source is now
unrepresentable: it has to be reclassified as internal, which is a claim someone makes in
writing rather than a line that quietly disappears.
A SIXTH instance, found by auditing this file's own classifications rather than by a bug
report. The question that found it: which constants are named ONLY by files classified
internal-only, and of those which does the shim not declare? Ten, and eight were WebGL 2
pixel-store parameters that content sets through pixelStorei -- so the classification of
backend/gl/state_tracker.rs as internal was itself the blind spot. A constant named only
by an internal file is never checked, which is exactly what makes a wrong internal_only
entry costly rather than merely untidy. Re-run that audit after editing internal_only.

sources.engine/crates/graphics/src/renderergl/ha: The GL command executor: every WebGL call content makes arrives here, and every enum it returns leaves here.
sources.engine/crates/graphics/src/webgl_gpu_bud: The engine's own list of sized internal formats it accounts for, which is therefore the set content may pass to texStorage/renderbufferStorage/texImage.
sources.engine/crates/graphics/src/canvas/manage: Owns the framebuffer and texture objects content binds, so it names the binding-point and query enums.
sources.engine/crates/graphics/src/device_caps.r: Capability detection; what it reads is what getParameter can report.
sources.engine/crates/graphics/src/compressed_up: Compressed texture upload, reached by content through compressedTexImage2D.
sources.engine/crates/graphics/src/texture_impor: Texture import paths content reaches through texImage2D with an external source.
sources.engine/crates/graphics/src/backend/gl/st: Shadows the GL state content sets so redundant calls can be skipped -- which makes it a content boundary, not an internal one. Classified internal at first, and that was wrong: the eight WebGL 2 pixel-store parameters are named here and nowhere else, so the misclassification left the only file that names them unchecked and content could not name them either.

not_exposed_by_webgl.INFO_LOG_LENGTH: WebGL has no length query: getShaderInfoLog and getProgramInfoLog return a string, so the executor reads this length to size its own buffer and content never names it.
not_exposed_by_webgl.SHADER_SOURCE_LENGTH: Same shape as INFO_LOG_LENGTH, for getShaderSource.
not_exposed_by_webgl.EXTENSIONS: WebGL replaces the GL string query with getSupportedExtensions(), which is implemented. Declaring the enum would offer content a getParameter path WebGL does not define.
not_exposed_by_webgl.DRAW_FRAMEBUFFER_BINDING: GLES 3 gives it the same enum as FRAMEBUFFER_BINDING (0x8CA6), which is declared. A second name for one enum would imply two queries where there is one.
not_exposed_by_webgl.PROGRAM_BINARY_LENGTH: WebGL exposes no program-binary API: getProgramBinary/programBinary are GLES calls with no WebGL counterpart and no extension that adds one. The shader cache uses this to size its own buffer, and content has no way to ask for a binary at all.
not_exposed_by_webgl.NUM_PROGRAM_BINARY_FORMATS: Same as PROGRAM_BINARY_LENGTH: WebGL has no program-binary API, so there is nothing for content to enumerate formats for.

internal_only.engine/crates/graphics/src/atlas/mod.rs: Glyph and image atlas allocation. Content never names an atlas, let alone its formats.
internal_only.engine/crates/graphics/src/canvas/manage: Canvas2D's own GL use. Canvas2D's content-facing surface is strings and numbers, not GL enums.
The onscreen drawing buffer the engine owns. Content sees a canvas, not this.
Pixel-buffer upload internals, including the engine's own fences. Content's fences go through the executor.
Descriptor types for engine-owned GL objects.
Damage tracking; the one enum is for the engine's own scissor use.
internal_only.engine/crates/graphics/src/frame_capture: Frame capture for tests and the player's --offscreen path, not a content API.
Shader binary caching; content names shaders, never the cache's enums.
internal_only.engine/crates/graphics/src/upload_thread: The upload thread's own GL work and fences.
